body: Much better approach in my opinion. It's good that this is not exposed to the public API.

Interesting that this PR uses `int32_t` for unique node IDs, but we already use Strings for resource UIDs.

Since this is intended to be useful for the 3D asset pipeline, is the intention to pitch to Khronos that unique node IDs use 32-bit integers in glTF? What about non-node unique IDs, like meshes having unique IDs? If we get a glTF unique ID extension, then that should apply to all items within a glTF file including nodes and resources. I would expect that Strings would be a more agnostic approach that would match resources and work the same across engines.

> If a scene renames or moves a node, inherited or instantiated scenes will no longer lose reference to it.

What does that mean exactly? In what situation can a node disappear and get recovered? I don't see the IDs used anywhere other than Nodes' headers in the scene.

> In what situation can a node disappear and get recovered?

When nodes in a inherit**ed** scene are renamed or moved, inherit**ing** scenes are not aware of the change. As such, changes applied to inheriting scenes may be lost. This is a notorious issue as it discourages scene inheritance.

You can also argue this is, in part, a consequence of no refactoring tools or automation on the editor side.
It seems though that, based on the existing UID implementation, reduz would rather enforce hard references than letting the editor figure it out (eh)

> When nodes in a inherited scene are renamed or moved, inheriting scenes are not aware of the change. As such, changes applied to inheriting scenes may be lost. This is a notorious issue as it discourages scene inheritance.

Ah yeah, makes sense.

I only tested whether nodes under editable children would disappear and it's still a problem, and it's btw what #73911 tries to solve. Not sure if it's planned? Another thing that IDs could fix, and they don't right now, are NodePath properties that become invalid when a node is moved externally. It's especially relevant for animations.

Here's a MRP which can be used to reproduce the issue of losing local child nodes parented to an inherited scene's node (via Editable Children). This PR properly solves this issue (provided that the scenes have been saved at least once with this PR merged to save the unique node IDs).

[BugReproSceneComposition.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20993694/BugReproSceneComposition.zip)

This scenario is described in a handful of issues I've seen in the past. I don't have time now to do a deep search, but it would be good if someone did to list which issues would be solved by this PR (or which ones could be but aren't).

---

I found an edge case though, seen in this modified version of the MRP:

[BugReproSceneComposition2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20993849/BugReproSceneComposition2.zip)

With this setup:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f547075-3f93-44da-bf5e-64f22d9097bf)

In `ItemScene`, I rename `Player` to `PlayerOld`, then save.
If the `MainScene` is then opened, the `NodeAddedFromMainScene` properly stays parented to the `PlayerOld`. **Don't save `MainScene`.**
In `ItemScene`, I rename the Node2D `Other` to `Player`, then save.
If the `MainScene` is still open (but not saved), it shows the expected parenting still. But if it's closed/reopened, then the `parent="Player"` attribute takes precedence and the `NodeAddedFromMainScene` node gets parented to the new (Node2D) `Player`.

It's a bit of a corner case but I could see it happen occasionally due to the fact that our nodes have a default name, so it's easy enough to get name conflicts/reuse old names after rename.
E.g. you may add a Sprite2D named `Sprite2D`, parent something to it where it's inherited, then later rename that sprite to e.g. `HandSprite`, while adding a new sibling sprite (e.g. for an overlay) and keep it with its default name `Sprite2D`. Doing this kind of edit is pretty common and if done at the same time, external nodes might get wrongly reparented.

This seems to be due to this part of the design:

> - These IDs act as a fallback to names when saving.
> - The IDs are USED AS A FALLBACK, so they are just an addition. It should not break any current existing scene.

Why can't we use them as the first source of truth *if they exist*, instead of using them as fallback only? If they don't exist, we should fall back silently to using `parent` like usual, so it should also not break existing scenes.

> When nodes in a inherited scene are renamed or moved, inheriting scenes are not aware of the change. As such, changes applied to inheriting scenes may be lost. This is a notorious issue as it discourages scene inheritance.

Some answers to comments above:

@akien-mga 
> Why can't we use them as the first source of truth if they exist, instead of using them as fallback only? If they don't exist, we should fall back silently to using parent like usual, so it should also not break existing scenes.

@Ivorforce 
> General question: Is it really safe to fall back to unique IDs when the parent instantiated scene changes? What if the structural changes imply a change to how the nodes should be stored? Perhaps trying to restore is better than not trying, but it doesn't feel foolproof.

Its just actually just a lot easier to mess up if IDs were the primary source of truth. This is what I tried in my previous PR (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/86960). If you have an inherited scene, user could have copied and have duplicated IDs (used in instances or whathever in the base scene). That would be near impossible to figure out or fix for the user if broken. Text format would become so cryptic that it would be unusable to fix manually.

This is why, this approach relies on strings _first_, and if not found it will rely on IDs. So, if IDs are messed up, nothing really happens. It's not 100% foolproof, but I don't think its really possible to do so (or worth the effort). To put it in other words:
* In the far most common cases, this PR just fixes the most common problems and does not create new ones. 
* By using IDs first, you have the potential of creating _new_ problems that did not exist before.

Here are a couple test projects I've used with this PR rebased on `master`:
1. Renaming/reparenting nodes with no overridden properties (fixed): [BugReproSceneComposition.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22666478/BugReproSceneComposition.zip)
2. Renaming with name collision (~fixed~ *Edit:* Tested again and it's actually still buggy): [BugReproSceneComposition2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22666481/BugReproSceneComposition2.zip)
3. Renaming/reparenting nodes with overridden properties, inherited or instantiated (not fixed): [inherited-scenes-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22666432/inherited-scenes-test.zip)

The first two are fixed by this PR and are situations where nodes get renamed and potential *other* nodes that were added to them in a parent scene with Editable Children get lost. This is a scenario where one uses Editable Children to do composition by adding new components as nodes under them in a scene.

For clarity, to benefit from unique node IDs for refactoring, all scenes need to be re-saved once after building this PR, so that the unique node IDs get generated and written to the scenes. If there's no unique node ID in the scene, the functionality obviously cannot be used.

The third project (modified from #100038) shows the case KoBeWi exemplified as not fixed, and IMO that's indeed a big miss to make this PR really useful, and worth adding unique node IDs everywhere: keeping parent/child relationship across renames is great, but if overridden properties are lost, it's still making the inherited scene and Editable Children workflows pretty unreliable. @reduz suggests it may not be too hard to solve this part with the work done here for node unique IDs, so I suggest we get this implemented in this PR before merging.

> Renaming/reparenting nodes with overridden properties, inherited or instantiated (not fixed): [inherited-scenes-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22666432/inherited-scenes-test.zip)

So this was still not fixed in the MRP because the previous version of the PR only shared the unique ID for inherited scenes created with the changes from that PR. Pre-existing inherited scenes would have separate IDs and so while renaming works, properties would be lost. There were also issues when a scene is instantiated multiple times in a scene and unique IDs for related child nodes could not be shared due to conflicts.

We did a bit of testing and iteration with Juan and now it works, all inherited and instantiated (with editable children) nodes properly share the relevant IDs with the scene they inherit/instantiate. Juan says he actually came up to a technically correct solution now and not a hack, so it might also be more reliable.

I'll do some more testing ASAP and try to identify which open bug reports are closed by this PR.

Did some more testing and I confirmed that this fixes a lot of issues reported over the years. I linked the ones which I could find and which are still open in the OP. While testing I found a regression from addressing the last review comment, which broke preserving data when reparenting. I fixed it up. There's one last issue I could find but it's very niche, so I think it's fine to merge this PR without addressing it. It could likely be addressed in a follow-up using the unique Node IDs introduced by this PR. The problem is shown in https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22666481/BugReproSceneComposition2.zip I shared above: If you rename the Node `Player` to `PlayerOld`, and the Node2D `Other` to `Player` and save the parent scene, the instantiated one will wrongly see its `NodeAddedFromMainScene` reparented from the Node to the Node2D (i.e. from the old `Player` to the new `Player`). Instead of relying on paths, it should check the unique node ID for that. But maybe that would be too expensive in the normal case where paths don't get swapped? Workaround: Do this kind of name swapping in two steps. Rename `Player`, save both scenes, then rename `Other` to `Player`. Saving the scene where the renamed node is instantiated lets it update its saved paths using the node IDs.

Hi, if you'd like to access unique node IDs through the GDScript / GDExtension APIs, please [open a proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals?tab=readme-ov-file#how-to-suggest-improvements) where you describe your use-case for it.

It would be nice to see this unique ID saved and exposed at runtime. For a save-system that is forced to use node-path as the unique identifier for objects to read their state with on a load we run the risk of making an edit to a game and blowing up a user's save-file if we've changed the tree in any way. If this ID was available it would alleviate the same problems at run-time that this PR addresses at design-time.
Again, please don't comment this here; open a proposal (discussion or concrete issue) instead.
